hypotheses.title: Build-State Evidence remains the strongest single-project bet
hypotheses.statement: If the archive must recommend one broad buildable contribution, Build-State Evidence remains the strongest candidate because compile, rebuild, and resource-usage taxes remain broadly felt while Cargo is actively moving toward recorded machine-usable build evidence rather than a finished review product.
leading_indicators: Cargo-native build-analysis and report surfaces keep getting more useful without already closing the review gap
compile/rebuild/resource pain remains one of the most common broad taxes
downstream build, review, and diagnosis tools still benefit from explicit build receipts
downgrade_triggers: Cargo-native report surfaces already satisfy most review and operator needs without a meaningful companion layer
broad ecosystem pain shifts decisively away from build and rebuild evidence toward another seam
falsifiers: A clearly broader and more buildable single-project seam repeatedly outperforms Build-State across representative packets, pilots, and proving grounds
Upstream Cargo ships enough integrated reviewable build evidence that the proposed companion layer becomes mostly redundant
notes: This is a ranking claim, not permission for Build-State to absorb intake, qualification, or navigation work wholesale.

hypotheses.title: A thin family of evidence, review, and readiness layers remains stronger than one new platform empire
hypotheses.statement: The strongest coordinated answer is still a thin family led by Build-State Evidence, Package Intake + Release Boundary Review, Debug Acceptance, Compatibility Claims, and Safety-Critical / Institutional Readiness rather than one hosted control plane or one universal framework.
leading_indicators: The strongest seams keep showing distinct imported truths, operator verbs, and steward homes
Cargo and service surfaces continue to expose raw facts while leaving richer review products companion-shaped
No one product surface can absorb build review, intake review, debugger acceptance, readiness cards, and renewable claims honestly
downgrade_triggers: One layer repeatedly proves decorative rather than decision-bearing across packets and pilots
A single narrower combination repeatedly covers the same operator decisions with materially less residue
falsifiers: Representative pilots show that a substantially smaller family covers the same practical decisions with lower maintenance cost
A single coherent upstream/service substrate emerges that honestly handles most of the family without hiding negative states
notes: This is a family-shape claim, not a claim that one team should build all layers at once.

hypotheses.title: Fast substrate drift should land in watchcards before anyone treats it as frontier promotion
hypotheses.statement: Fresh Cargo, crates.io, docs.rs, or machine-readable-surface movement should usually refresh watchcards or packets first; it should not count as a new frontier or a broad ladder rewrite until multiple independent signals say the old strategic read is materially wrong.
leading_indicators: New signals mostly alter imported facts, caveats, or operator boundary details rather than the broad priority map
The best next move keeps being watchcard or packet refresh rather than seam promotion
The broad leaders continue to fit the fresh evidence
downgrade_triggers: Multiple fresh sources consistently point to a different broad leader or an obviously missing frontier
Watchcards repeatedly accumulate changes that packets and canon cannot honestly absorb without a broader rewrite
falsifiers: Independent official sources repeatedly show that the current broad ladder is materially wrong, not just in need of caveats
A new specialist or broad seam repeatedly dominates representative packets, proving grounds, and buildout decisions
notes: This is a posture claim about revision discipline, not a promise that the map never changes.

hypotheses.title: The anti-tacit-knowledge answer is evidence-bearing navigation and defaults, not a giant portal
hypotheses.statement: Adoption navigation remains strategically important, but the worthy answer is still receipt-bearing defaults, routeable guidance, and scoped atlas work rather than a giant ecosystem portal, recommendation engine, or assistant-memory canon.
leading_indicators: Docs and maintainer-authored guidance remain the main canonical learning channel
Navigation pain keeps showing up as tacit-knowledge and decision-framing trouble, not just missing search
Renewal burden keeps dominating bigger atlas or portal proposals
downgrade_triggers: A smaller, renewable portal-like shape repeatedly proves honest and maintainable across real teams
Navigation work repeatedly delivers more value through centralized discovery than through local receipts and defaults
falsifiers: Representative adoption pilots show that a portal-first or assistant-memory-first layer solves more of the navigation burden with acceptable renewal cost and explicit negative-state handling
Maintainer-authored defaults and receipt-bearing guidance repeatedly fail to improve real decisions even when renewed honestly
notes: This card protects against overcorrecting toward giant discovery products just because tacit knowledge is real.

hypotheses.title: Evidence and boundary-review layers should usually land before broader atlas or policy surfaces
hypotheses.statement: The archive should still stage build-state evidence and package/release-boundary review ahead of broader atlas/default, qualification, or specialist recommendation surfaces, because current Rust movement is making raw facts and service truth more concrete before it is making broad policy layers cheap to renew.
leading_indicators: Build and package-boundary surfaces keep getting fresher upstream and service-side hooks
Broader atlas and qualification surfaces still carry larger renewal or stewardship burdens
Teams can make useful local decisions earlier on evidence and review layers than on bigger portal or program claims
downgrade_triggers: Broader atlas or readiness-program layers begin shipping with lower renewal burden and stronger direct decision value than the evidence layers
The leading evidence layers stop compounding into downstream decisions
falsifiers: Representative work shows that atlas/default or readiness-program layers consistently deliver more immediate decision value than evidence and boundary-review layers even without those layers in place
The evidence layers stop being a practical prerequisite for broader operator or institutional decisions
notes: This is a sequencing claim, not a denial that navigation or readiness work matters strategically.

hypotheses.title: Fresh signals should refresh the smallest honest loop, not a blended prose layer
hypotheses.statement: When fresh official signals arrive, the archive should refresh the smallest honest loop—watchcard, packet, stewardship, canon, or hygiene—instead of collapsing everything into one “latest thinking” prose pass.
leading_indicators: Most fresh changes keep fitting one dominant loop cleanly
The repo stays easier to maintain when watchcards, packets, and canon changes remain visibly separate
Source-candor failures fall when revisions explicitly say what did not change
downgrade_triggers: Multiple revisions repeatedly require synchronized changes across almost every loop
The loop model stops helping readers predict where fresh evidence should land
falsifiers: The smallest-loop rule repeatedly produces misleading fragmentation and a blended artifact would be more honest
Future Rust process signals move away from cadence- and owner-shaped work toward one dominant always-current surface
notes: This is a repo-hygiene claim, not a claim that each revision must touch only one artifact family.

hypotheses.title: Machine-readable and service-side truths only help when their caveats travel with them
hypotheses.statement: Machine-readable surfaces such as Cargo report/build metadata, rustdoc JSON, libtest JSON, and service-hosted docs or registry facts are high-value inputs, but they only remain trustworthy when explicit caveats about versioning, incompleteness, unsupported states, and scope travel with them.
leading_indicators: Sources continue to publish strong structured outputs but also explicit warnings about compatibility or completeness
Companion tools keep benefiting from imported facts while still needing negative-state receipts and caveats
Fresh drift keeps happening first at the format or service-boundary level
downgrade_triggers: Key machine-readable surfaces stabilize enough that caveat burden drops materially
Consumers can repeatedly treat those surfaces as durable contracts without significant qualification overhead
falsifiers: Upstream and service operators provide stable compatibility guarantees that make most of the archive's current caveat discipline obsolete
Companion tools repeatedly succeed by ignoring caveats without harming trust or operator decisions
notes: This card is anti-smoothing: it exists to keep useful machine truth from being oversold.

hypotheses.title: Safety-critical and institutional readiness remains program-shaped rather than crate-shaped
hypotheses.statement: Safety-critical and institutional readiness remains a commons/program seam whose practical bottlenecks are qualification discipline, evidence renewal, target and dependency policy, and durable stewardship rather than the absence of one more crate.
leading_indicators: Qualification, FLS/spec, and ecosystem-readiness work keep requiring multi-party maintenance rather than one product release
Industrial and safety users keep needing dependency policy, evidence cards, and long-lived replacement plans
Foundation or project-level hosting/support structures remain relevant to this seam
downgrade_triggers: A bounded product or tool family repeatedly solves most safety-readiness friction without large stewardship residue
Qualification-oriented needs become much more commoditized inside upstream or vendor tooling
falsifiers: Representative safety-critical adoption stories stop hinging on stewardship, qualification, or lifecycle governance and instead collapse into an ordinary crate/tool purchase
The commons/program layer repeatedly fails to improve practical readiness even when renewed honestly
notes: This is a shape claim about the seam, not a promise that one consortium or foundation vehicle is automatically the right steward.
